claim: Under strict scoring all 18 model-strategy cells have negative NCE (overconfidence) on a shared post-cutoff LiveCodeBench window.
stance_target: verbal confidence on code is overconfident
scope_conditions: 6 instruct coder models, LCB v6 365 problems, self-assessment
quoted_support: All eighteen strict-scoring NCE point estimates are negative, and seventeen of the corresponding 95% percentile bootstrap intervals remain below zero.

breadth.confidence_families: verbalized only: Direct numeric, CoT-then-score, Linguistic labels (Sec 3.3); logprob/probe not run (Sec 2 says intrinsic not studied)
breadth.base_vs_instruct: not present: instruction-tuned only (Sec 3.2); no base counterparts
breadth.reasoning_models: not present (searched: reasoning; CoT prompting only, Sec 3.3; no reasoning-mode models)
breadth.elicitation_formats: Direct 0-100 integer; CoT then FINAL_CONFIDENCE; 5 ordered linguistic labels mapped to 10/30/50/70/90 (Sec 3.3, App B); repair call for malformed outputs
breadth.label_source: hidden test execution, strict all-tests-pass (Sec 3.1); lenient 10% tolerance secondary
breadth.label_independence: code frozen before elicitation, same model self-assesses (Sec 3.3); labels independent of confidence pass
breadth.contamination_split: shared post-cutoff window; Qwen cutoff proxied by tech-report date 2024-09-18; not per-model release-date splits (Sec 3.1)
breadth.calibration_metrics: ECE 10 equal-width bins, NCE, AUROC, AUACC, PRR with tie averaging, Platt scaling diagnostic, 1,000 bootstrap (Sec 3.5)
breadth.causal_intervention: not present (searched: intervention, ablation of internals)

claim: ECE and AUROC decouple across cells: lowest ECE 0.013 coincides with AUROC 0.491, highest AUROC 0.841 has ECE 0.216.
stance_target: calibration and discrimination of verbal confidence must be reported separately
quoted_support: The lowest ECE in the table is 0.013 for CodeLlama-7B Linguistic, whose AUROC is 0.491, while the highest AUROC is 0.841 for Qwen2.5-Coder-32B Linguistic, whose ECE is 0.216.

claim: 8 of 18 verbalized-confidence cells have collapsed distributions (>=50% of mass in one of 20 histogram bins) and 5 are unstable across 5 repeated elicitations.
stance_target: favorable ECE can be an artifact of collapse
quoted_support: Eight of the 18 combinations are collapsed and five are unstable across repeated runs, including three Chain-of-Thought combinations.

claim: Confidence-ranked review (least confident first) beats random in all cells only for the best model; tie-averaged PRR ranges from -0.029 to 0.705 across cells.
stance_target: verbal confidence has weak ranking utility for most small coder models
scope_conditions: Table 2; whole-solution; review-ordering only, not execution-budget routing
quoted_support: Direct elicitation gives the largest improvement over random selection in four of six models.

quoted_support: In contrast, no existing work compares black-box verbalized elicitation strategies across multiple coding-specialized LLMs on a shared temporally filtered window.
